claimText: When an aircraft on the same track is cleared to climb or descend through the level of another aircraft, the clearance should be issued provided the following requirements are met: longitudinal distance determined by ground automation from near-simultaneous demand ADS-C reports with position accuracy of 0.25 NM or better; longitudinal distance not less than 27.8 km (15 NM) or 46.3 km (25 NM) depending on speed; altitude difference not greater than 600 m (2 000 ft); clearance issued with restriction ensuring vertical separation re-established within 15 minutes; and direct controller-pilot voice communications or CPDLC maintained.
rationale: Guidance ('should') for CDP clearance issuance conditions.
exactSourceQuotes: When an aircraft on the same track is cleared to climb or descend through the level of another aircraft, the clearance should be issued provided the following requirements are met:

the longitudinal distance between the aircraft is determined by the ground automation system from near-simultaneous demand ADS-C reports which contain position accuracy of 0.25 NM or better (Figure of Merit 6 or higher);

the longitudinal distance between the aircraft, as determined in a) above, is not less than: 1) 27.8 km (15 NM) when the preceding aircraft is at the same speed or faster than the following aircraft; or 2) 46.3 km (25 NM) when the following aircraft is not more than either 18.5 km/h (10 kt) or Mach 0.02 faster than the preceding aircraft;
the altitude difference between aircraft is not greater than 600 m (2 000 ft);
the clearance is issued with a restriction that ensures vertical separation is re-established within 15 minutes from the first demand report request;
direct controller-pilot voice communications or CPDLC is maintained.
